purpose: private authored activity pilot; not learner-facing

activities.cueEnglish: Find what the worker notices about the lifeline.
activities.modelFrench: Pendant le travail sur le toit, un ouvrier remarque un problème avec la ligne de vie.
activities.modelEnglish: While they work on the roof, a worker sees something wrong with the lifeline.

activities.cueEnglish: Without looking, name the competent person in French.
Listen and identify the French word for lanyard.
Type 'Where is the competent person?' in French.
State that the anchor appears unsafe.
activities.modelFrench: Le contremaître dit : « Arrêtez le travail. Cet ancrage semble dangereux. »
activities.modelEnglish: The foreman says: Stop work. The anchor is not safe.

activities.cueEnglish: Write what the competent person confirms in the scene.
activities.modelFrench: La personne compétente inspecte le système et confirme la distance libre de chute requise.
activities.modelEnglish: The competent person does the inspection and confirms the fall distance of the system.

activities.cueEnglish: Find what makes the roof slippery in the morning.
activities.modelFrench: Cherchez un appui stable, car la rosée rend le toit glissant.
activities.modelEnglish: Look for solid footing, because the dew makes the roof slippery.

activities.cueEnglish: Without looking, name lightning in French.
Listen and identify the French word for storm.
Type 'A storm is coming. Come down now.' in French.
activities.modelEnglish: A storm is coming. Come down now.

activities.cueEnglish: Tell the crew that the roof is wet.
activities.modelFrench: Le contremaître prévient l’équipe : « Le toit est mouillé. Faites attention. »
activities.modelEnglish: The foreman warns: The roof is wet. Be careful.

activities.cueEnglish: Write what changes in the sky later in the scene.
activities.modelFrench: Plus tard, le vent se lève et des nuages sombres apparaissent dans le ciel.
activities.modelEnglish: Later, the wind picks up and dark clouds appear in the sky.

activities.cueEnglish: Find how Raúl answers the dizziness question.
activities.modelFrench: Raúl répond que oui, un peu.

activities.cueEnglish: Without looking, name heat exhaustion in French.
Listen and identify the French phrase for dizziness.
Type 'How do you feel?' in French.
Ask Raúl directly whether he is dizzy.
Write what the foreman says about the site heat plan.
activities.modelFrench: « Dites-moi si vous vous sentez mal, et nous suivrons le plan chaleur du chantier. »
activities.modelEnglish: Tell me if you feel sick, and we will follow the site heat plan.
